title: Icici Bank Ltd. With Its vs M/S National Dairies Products on 24 December, 2011
full_text: Icici Bank Ltd. With Its vs M/S National Dairies Products on 24 December, 2011 IN THE COURT OF SHRI ARUN KUMAR, METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE:DWARKA COURTS:NEW DELHI CC NO: 3611/10 Unique Case ID No: 0240SR1014832003 ICICI Bank Ltd. with its, Registered Office at Landmark, Race Course Circle, Vadodara­390007 and one of its branches functioning at F­42, Kamla Nagar, Delhi­110007 ..............Complainant Versus 1. M/s National Dairies Products, 16/9995, New Rohtak Road, New Delhi­110005 Also to be served at :­ 2. Shri Vishal Ahliwalia, Partner/Authorised Signatory M/s National Dairies Products New Delhi­110005. Also to be served at:­ CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 1 of 29 UC­26/C­9, White House Town, DLF Phase­III, Gurgaon, Haryana. 3. Smt. Raksha Ahluwalia, Partner, M/s National Dairies Products, 16/9995, New Rohtak Road, New Delhi­110005. Also to be served at:­ U­26­C­9, White House Town, DLF Phase­III, Gurgaon, Haryana. ................Accused Date of filing : 03.06.2003 Date of Institution : 05.06.2003 Date of reserving judgment/order : 13.12.2011 Offence Complained of or proved : Under section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act,1881 Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty Final Order/Judgment : Accused no. 2 convicted Accused no. 3 acquitted Date of pronouncement : 24.12.2011 JUDGMENT: BRIEF FACTS AND REASONS FOR THE DECISION OF THE CASE:­ CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 2 of 29 1. Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of the present complaint u/s 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act filed by Bank of Rajasthan, a Company incorporated under the Mewar Companies Act, 1942 now deemed to be registered under Companies Act, 1956 against M/s National Dairies Products, a partnership firm and against its partners. During the pendency of the present complaint, M/s Bank of Rajasthan Ltd. has amalgamated with the ICICI Bank Ltd., pursuant to the Scheme of Amalgamation of the Bank of Rajasthan Ltd. with ICICI Bank Ltd. sanctioned by the Reserve Bank of India vide its order dated August 12,2010 and accordingly, on an application, moved on behalf of the complainant bank, the name of the complainant was changed from M/s Bank of Rajasthan Ltd. to M/s ICICI Bank Ltd. vide order dated 05.03.2011 passed by Ld. Predecessor of this Court. 2. The case of the complainant as per the complaint is that the complainant bank served a notice u/s 13(2) and 13(13) of the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act 2002, (hereinafter referred to as SARFAESI Act ) for the outstanding liability in the account of accused nos. 1,2,3 apart from another guarantor namely Shri Sanjay Gupta and since the accused persons failed to make the payment of the outstanding amount in the CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 3 of 29 account, a receiver was appointed by the Court of Ld. CMM, Delhi vide order dated 13.03.2003 for taking over of the possession of secured assets in terms of SARFAESI Act . According to the complainant, when the receiver appointed by Ld. CMM, Delhi alongwith the official of the complainant reached to the shop of accused no. 1, on 26.03.2003, the accused no. 1 issued a cheque bearing No. 459696 dated 28.03.2003 for a sum of Rs. 5,00,000/­ in favour of the complainant in consideration of liability outstanding in the account of accused persons alongwith letter dated 26.03.2003 with the assurance that the same will be honored on its presentation and in view of the aforesaid assurance, process of taking over of the possession of secured assets was deferred. The cheque was signed by accused no.2 as the authorised signatory of accused no.1. According to the complainant, on presentation the aforesaid cheque was returned unpaid by the banker of the accused vide cheque return memo dated 29.03.2003 with the remarks "Insufficient Funds", which was received by the complainant on 31.03.2003. Thereafter, complainant informed the accused that the cheque given by him has bounced and the accused promised to pay the amount but failed to pay the same and accordingly, legal notice dated 07.04.2003 u/s 138 of the NI Act was served upon the accused demanding the payment of cheque amount but CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 4 of 29 the accused neither replied to the legal notice , nor paid the amount of the said cheque and ultimately, the present complaint u/s 138 of the NI Act has been filed by the complainant allegedly through its duly authorised representative Mr. Pradeep Jain. It is submitted by the complainant that all the accused persons are liable to be punished u/s 138 of the NI Act as the accused no.1 is the borrower, the accused no.2 is the partner as well as authorised signatory of accused no.1 and accused no.3 is the partner of accused no.1 and accused no.2 & 3 are looking after the day to day conduct of business of accused no.1. 3. The accused were summoned vide order dated 27.08.2003, whereupon the accused have entered appearance through their Counsel on 20.12.2003 and notice u/s 251 Cr.P.C . were thereafter issued to accused no. 2 and to accused no.3 through her Counsel on 18.03.2005 to which both the accused have not pleaded guilty and claimed trial and the matter was fixed for complainant's evidence. 4. The complainant has examined two witnesses in support of its case. Mr. Pradeep Jain, AR of the complainant, has been examined as CW­1 who has tendered the evidence by way of affidavit, in support of submissions made in the complaint. Shri Anupam Goel, an official of the banker of accused has been examined as CW­2, who has proved the CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 5 of 29 cheque return memos EX.CW1/7 and Ex. CW1/8 and has also produced the statement of account of the accused which is EX.CW2/1. The complainant has relied upon the following documents:­ EX.CW1/1: Power of Attorney in favour of Shri Pradeep Jain, AR of the complainant. EX.CW1/2(Colly): Notice u/s 13(2) and 13(13) of the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act 2002. EX.CW1/3: Order dated 13.03.2003 appointing a receiver from the Court of Ld. CMM, Delhi. EX.CW1/4: Letter of assurance dated 26.03.2003 given by accused in favour of the complainant. EX.CW1/5: Original Cheque bearing No. 459697 dated 15.04.2003 for a sum of Rs. 2,00,000/­ drawn on Hansalaya, 15, Barakhamba Road, New Delhi Branch of ABN Amro Bank NV. EX.CW1/6: Original Cheque bearing No. 459698 dated 18.04.2003 for a sum of Rs. 3,00,000/­ drawn on Hansalaya, 15, Barakhamba Road, New Delhi Branch of ABN Amro Bank NV. EX.CW1/7: Cheque returning Memo dated 17.04.2003. EX.CW1/8: Cheque returning Memo dated 21.04.2003. CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 6 of 29 EX.CW1/9: Legal Notice dated 30.04.2003. EX.CW1/10 to EX.CW1/14: Original postal receipts bearing no. 2697 to 2701 dated 01.05.2003. EX.CW1/15 to EX.CW1/19: Original UPC Receipts dated 01.05.2003. EX.CW1/20 to EX.CW1/24: Envelops received back. EX.CW2/1: Statement of bank account of the accused maintained by the accused with the drawee bank. Thereafter, the accused no.2 was examined u/s 313 of the Cr.P.C. on 15.02.2007 on behalf of himself and on behalf of accused no.3 as authorised vide letter dated 14.02.2007 and the matter was fixed for defence evidence. 5. The accused no. 2 has examined himself as a defence witness with the permission of this Court and relied on the letter of verification regarding the payments allegedly made by him towards the cheque amount in question and statement of account of the accused for the relevant period which are DW1/1 & DW1/2 respectively. Accused has also relied on the copies of DDs and acknowledgment regarding issuance of draft in sum of Rs. 5,00,000/­ and copy of receipt regarding deposit of aforesaid drafts with the complainant which are EX.DW1/3 to CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 7 of 29 EX.CDW1/6 respectively. 6. Thereafter on statement of Accused no.2 defence evidence was closed vide order dated 03.09.2011 and the matter was fixed for final arguments. 7. Final arguments in the case were heard on 19.09.2011 and the matter was fixed for pronouncement of judgment. Written submissions on behalf of the complainant had also been filed by Ld. Counsel for the complainant. At that stage, it came to the notice of this court that the accused no. 3 was not examined under Section 313 of the Cr.P.C. and on the basis of authorization letter given by accused no. 3 in favour of accused number 2, the statement of accused number 2 was recorded on behalf of accused number 3. Moreover during the said examination, certain incriminating evidence against accused number 3 could not be put to the alleged AR of the accused no. 3. Therefore, the court vide order dated 10.10.2011 decided to examine the accused number 3 under Section 313 of the Cr.P.C. afresh and accordingly the accused number 3 was examined under Section 313 of the Cr.P.C. On 21.11.2011. Thereafter, the accused No. 3 examined herself in her defence after moving an application in writing under Section 315 of the Cr.P.C. and after cross examination of accused number 3, DE was closed on a CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 8 of 29 separate statement of accused number 3. Thereafter, final arguments on behalf of all the parties were heard afresh on 13.12.2011 on which date additional written submissions were filed on behalf of the complainant, who chose not to advance any further oral arguments. 8. It is submitted by Ld. Counsel for the complainant that the complainant has proved beyond reasonable doubt all the ingredients of offence u/s 138 of the NI Act against all the three accused. It is submitted by him that the complainant has proved that the accused owed a liability in excess of the cheques amount in question as on the date of presentation of the cheques and in partial discharge of the aforesaid liability, the accused has issued the cheques EX.CW1/5 and EX. CW1/6 in favour of the complainant, which on presentation, got dishonoured for reasons "Insufficient Funds" and immediately on receipt of cheque return memos, the complainant had issued the legal notice EX.CW1/9 to all the accused, which was sent to them through registered AD as well as UPC on the correct address of the accused and although the envelops sent through registered AD have been received back by the complainant but the legal notice has been duly served upon the accused through UPC. It is submitted by Ld. Counsel for the complainant that the complainant has not only examined CW­1 in support of the aforesaid submissions but CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 9 of 29 even the accused no. 2 has admitted in his statement u/s 313 of the Cr.P.C . that he was having the liability towards the complainant and had issued the cheques EX.CW1/5 and Ex. CW­1/6 in favour of the complainant, which on presentation were dishonoured due to insufficient funds and that he had received the legal notice. It is further submitted by Ld. Counsel for the complainant that the complainant has proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused has failed to make the payment of cheques amount in question within 15 days from receipt of notice and accordingly, present complaint has been filed by the complainant through its duly authorised representative within the prescribed period of limitation for filing the same. In view of the aforesaid facts, it is further submitted by him that the accused is liable to be convicted u/s 138 of the NI Act. 9. On the other hand, it is contended by Ld. Counsel for the accused that the complainant has utterly failed to prove that cheques EX.CW1/5 and EX. CW1/6 were issued by the accused in discharge of any liability towards the complainant. It is submitted by Ld. Counsel for the accused that no doubt the accused had outstanding liabilities towards the complainant under the two limits sanctioned in their favour by the complainant bank. However, according to him , the cheques EX.CW1/5 CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 10 of 29 and EX. CW1/6 were issued by the accused in favour of the complainant under a special arrangement as reflected in letter dated 26.03.2003 which is EX.CW1/4. According to him, the aforesaid cheques had been issued by the accused in favour of the complainant under the imminent pressure of the order passed by Ld. CMM, copy of which is EX.CW1/3 and in order to avoid the liability to hand over the possession of his shop, to the official receiver, in terms of the aforesaid order. According to him, since the object as well as the consideration for issuance of cheques EX.CW1/5and EX. CW1/6 as stated in letter dated 26.03.2003 issued by accused to the complainant and another letter dated 26.03.2003 issued by the complainant bank to the official receiver appointed by Ld. CMM, Delhi was unlawful, the aforesaid contract was void and as such, the accused cannot be held liable u/s 138 of the NI Act for dishonour of cheques issued in terms of a void contract. Even otherwise, it is submitted by him, the consequences of dishonour of the aforesaid cheques issued by the accused in favour of the complainant itself had been given the aforesaid letter EX.CW1/4, wherein it is stated that in case, the accused failed to honor the aforesaid or to submit the compromise proposal, he will hand over the possession of properties mortgaged to the bank. It is submitted by him that in fact the accused CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 11 of 29 had handed over the possession of the aforesaid shop to the complainant after dishonor of the aforesaid cheques in terms of the aforesaid undertaking given by him. It is further submitted by him that the complainant has failed to prove that legal notice was ever served on the accused particularly in view of the fact that envelops sent to the accused through registered AD have been placed on record by the complainant itself. Even otherwise it is submitted by him that the accused has already made payment to the complainant in respect of cheques amount in question in the month of December, 2003 and since the complainant has failed to prove the service of legal notice on the accused, the present complaint is not maintainable against the accused. 10. On the basis of aforesaid submissions following points arise for determination by this court. a) Whether the cheque Ex. CW­1/5 and Ex. CW­1/6 were issued by the accused in discharge of any legally enforceable debt or liability towards the complainant or not? b) Whether the legal demand notice under Section 138 of the NI Act was duly served on the accused or not? c) Whether the accused have made the payment towards cheques in question to the complainant within the statutory period of fifteen days? CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 12 of 29 d) Whether the present complaint is not maintainable qua accused number 3 in terms of Section 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act? I will deal with the aforesaid issues one by one. a) Whether the cheques Ex. CW­1/5 and Ex. CW­1/6 were issued by the accused in discharge of any legally enforceable debt or liability towards the complainant or not? 11. Before adverting to the first point for determination it would be apposite to reproduce the relevant portion of section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, which reads as follows: "138. Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency, etc., of funds in the account. ­ Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability, is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with that bank, such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence and shall, without prejudice to any other provision of this Act, be punished with CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 13 of 29 imprisonment for a term which may be extended to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both : Provided that nothing contained in this section shall apply unless ­ (a) the cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier; (b) the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, as the case may be, makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within thirty days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid; and (c) the drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money to the payee or as the case may be, to the holder in due course of the cheque, within fifteen days of the receipt of the said notice. Explanation :­ For the purposes of this section, `debt or other liability' means a legally enforceable debt or other liability." 12. In terms of the aforesaid Section, if a cheque issued by any person in discharge of any legally enforceable debt or liability is returned unpaid on presentation to the drawee bank for the reasons insufficiency of funds and despite service of demand notice, the drawer fails to make the CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 14 of 29 payment towards the cheque in question within fifteen days thereof and the complaint is filed within one month of such failure, the drawer and other person as referred to in Section 141 of the NI Act shall be liable to be punished under section 138 . Moreover, in terms of section 139 of the NI Act, once the signatures on the cheque are admitted by the drawer, there is a presumption that the cheque had been issued in discharge of any legally enforceable debt or liability although such presumption does not extend to the extent of presuming the existence of debt or liability. In the present case, the accused no. 2, has not only admitted the issuance of cheques Ex. CW­1/5 and Ex. CW­1/6 in favour of the complainant but has also admitted his liability towards the complainant. The only contention sought to be urged on behalf of the accused no. 2 is that the cheques were issued not in discharge of the aforesaid admitted liability under the two limits availed by accused no. 1 from the complainant, but the cheques were issued under a special arrangement i.e. in consideration of deferment of taking over of possession of the mortgaged property by the official receiver. Moreover, according to him, the aforesaid arrangement itself being void in view of the fact that object as well as consideration for issuance of cheques being unlawful, accused cannot be prosecuted for dishonour of the said cheques. Ld. Counsel for the CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 15 of 29 accused has heavily relied on the letter dated 26.03.2003 written by accused number 2 to the complainant bank and letter dated 26.03.2003 written by the complainant bank to the official receiver which are collectively marked as Ex. CW­1/4 in support of his submission that the cheques were given by the accused no. 2 to the complainant under the special arrangement in consideration for deferment of the taking over of the possession of the mortgaged property by the receiver. It is further submitted by him that in the aforesaid letter, the consequence of dishonour of the aforesaid cheques are also mentioned by the accused, i.e. in case of dishonour of the cheques, the accused shall handover the possession of the mortgaged property to the complainant. According to Ld. Counsel for the accused, immediately on dishonour of the aforesaid cheques, the accused no. 2 had actually handed over the possession of the mortgaged property to the complainant and, as such, had satisfied the consideration for issuance of the cheques in question. 13. On a perusal of material available on record, I do not find any substance in the aforesaid averment made by Ld. Counsel for the accused. It would be significant, at this stage, to reproduce the relevant portion of the letter written by accused no. 2, to the complainant which is marked as Ex. CW­1/4 which reads as follows: CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 16 of 29 "Sir I am giving three cheques as detailed:­ 1.Cheque No. 459696 amount Rs. 5,00,000/­ drawn ABN Amro dt. 28/3/03 2. Cheque No. 459697 amount Rs. 2,00,000/­ drawn ABN Amro dt. 15/04/03 3.Cheque No. 459698 amount Rs. 3,00,000/­ drawn ABN Amro dt. 18/04/03. Part liquidation of the said above A/C. I further undertake that I will give compromise proposal of the remaining amount acceptable to the bank within 30 days from the date hereof. In case I fail to honour the above mentioned or to submit compromise proposal as mentioned above, I myself will handover the property, plant/machinary charged/mortgaged to the bank. In view of the foregoing, I request you to please defer the taking of the possession of two months. I will be obliged. Thanking You Best Regards Sd/­" On a perusal of the aforesaid letter, admittedly written by the accused no. 2 to the complainant while handing over the cheques in question to the complainant, it is clear that the cheques in question were issued by the accused no.2 out of the account maintained by the accused no. 1 firm, in favour of the complainant in partial discharge of outstanding liabilities of his partnership firm towards the complainant in the two accounts maintained by the accused no. 1 firm with the CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 17 of 29 complainant bank. Since the purpose of taking over of the possession of the mortgaged property was to recover the outstandings against the accused from the sale proceeds of the same and since the accused had given the cheques in partial discharge of aforesaid liability and had given an undertaking to submit a proposal for settlement of the remaining amount, the request for deferring the taking over of possession was made by the complainant to the official receiver. Under the aforesaid facts and circumstances, it does not lie in the mouth of the accused to contend that, since upon dishonor of the cheques in question he had handed over the possession of the mortgaged property to the complainant, he is not liable to be prosecuted under Section 138 of the NI Act, as in my considered opinion, he was even otherwise bound in law to handover the possession of the mortgaged property to the official receiver, once an order in this regard had been passed by a competent court. In fact, the accused had successfully avoided the binding order of Ld. CMM for a considerable period of time, by issuing three cheques apparently without any intent to honour the same and hence had rendered himself liable for the prosecution under Section 138 of the NI Act, provided the other ingredients of offence are also established by the complainant. Thus in view of the aforesaid finding to the effect that the cheques Ex. CW­ CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 18 of 29 1/5and Ex. CW­1/6 were given by the accused no. 2 in part liquidation of liability of the accused no. 1 firm towards the complainant and not under any special arrangement as alleged by Ld. Counsel for the accused, I am not required to go into the issue as to whether the object and consideration of the aforesaid arrangement was lawful or unlawful. Hence the first question is answered in the affirmative. b) Whether the legal demand notice under Section 138 of the NI Act was duly served on all the accused or not? 14. It is submitted by Ld. Counsel for the complainant that the legal demand notice in terms of proviso (b) to Section 138 of the NI Act was duly served upon the accused in view of the fact that although the notice sent through registered AD post was returned unclaimed but the notice sent through UPC had never been received back by the complainant and despite service of the notice, the accused had failed to make the payment within the statutory period of 15 days and hence committed the offence under Section 138 of the NI Act. It is further submitted by Ld. Counsel for the complainant that not only the evidence led by the complainant regarding the service of legal notice on the accused remained uncontroverted during cross examination of AR of the complainant but even the accused number 2 has admitted during his examination under CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 19 of 29 Section 313 of the Cr.P.C. that he had received the legal notice. Thus according to Ld. Counsel for the complainant the aforesaid contention of the accused that legal notice was not served upon the accused is merely an afterthought and the accused has failed to rebut the presumption under section 27 of the General Clauses Act. On the other hand, it is submitted by Ld. Counsel for the Accused that the complainant has utterly failed to prove the service of the legal notice on the accused persons. According to him, the complainant itself has placed on record the returned envelopes meaning thereby that the legal notice was never served upon any of the accused. Moreover, according to him, Accused no. 3 has examined himself as DW­2 and has deposed on oath that she has not received the legal notice. I have considered the rival submissions made on behalf of both the parties and have perused the record. 15. It is well settled legal position that whenever any notice is sent through post by prepaying the postal charges and after properly addressing the same, there is a presumption not only under Section 27 of the General Clauses Act but also under Section 114 of the Evidence Act to the effect that the same must have been delivered to the addressee in the ordinary course. It is also well settled that the aforesaid presumptions not only arise in respect of articles sent through registered post CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 20 of 29 acknowledgment due but also in respect of the articles sent under postal certificate. However, the aforesaid presumptions are rebuttable in nature. 16. In the present case, the dispatch of the legal notice has been proved not only by the evidence of CW­1 by way of affidavit but also by placing on record the original postal receipts and by production of the postal certificate in respect of dispatch of notice through UPC. It was admitted by CW­1 that the legal notice sent through registered AD were received back undelivered with the remarks "premises was found locked despite repeated visits" and "not met", but according to Ld. Counsel for the complainant, the legal notice sent through UPC were never received back by the complainant. Besides, not only, no suggestion was given by Ld. Counsel for the accused to CW­1 to the effect that the legal notice was not received by the accused persons but also no suggestions to the effect that the postal receipts regarding the dispatch of the notice are forged have been given by him to the complainant's witness. Moreover, accused no. 2 has admitted in his examination under section 313 that he received the legal notice and although he stepped into the witness box as DW­1, he did not testify to the contrary. Although Accused no. 3 had denied in his examination in chief as DW­2 that she did not receive the legal notice, but both accused nos. 2 and 3 have admitted during their cross CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 21 of 29 examinations that the address mentioned in the legal notice and postal certificates is their correct address. DW­1 in his cross examination, in a response to query by Ld. Counsel for the accused as to whether he had received the legal notice or not has stated that "I do not remember". Similarly DW­2, during her cross examination, at one stage has stated that she does not know whether she received the legal notice or not, while admitting that the legal notice bears her correct address. Thus, in view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, in my considered view the accused have failed to rebut the presumption arising in favour of the complainant under Section 27 of the General Clauses Act and under Section 114 of the Evidence Act. Hence the Second question is answered in the affirmative. (c) Whether the accused have made the payment towards cheques in question to the complainant within the statutory period of fifteen days? 17. So far as the third issue is concerned the case of the complainant is that the accused have not only failed to make the payment towards the cheques in question within the statutory period of fifteen days from the date of service of notice but they have also failed to make the payment towards the cheques even till today. On the other hand, it is submitted by Ld. Counsel for the accused that accused have made the payment CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 22 of 29 towards the cheques in question to the complainant, in the month of December 2003 and since the complainant has failed to prove the service of legal notice upon the accused, there is no question of making any payment within the statutory period of fifteen days and hence in view of the aforesaid payments in the month of December 2003, the present complaint is not maintainable against either of the accused. In rebuttal it is submitted by Ld. Counsel for the complainant that although the accused had made the payments of Rs. 2,00,000/­, Rs. 3,00,000/­ and Rs. 5,00,000/­ on 12.11.2003, 18.12.2003 and 31.12.2003 respectively to the complainant, but the aforesaid payments were not made by the accused towards the dishonored cheques and the same were in partial discharge of their other liabilities towards the complainant. According to him, in any case, since the payments were not made by the accused within 15 days from the date of service of legal notice, the same does not absolve the accused of their liability under Section 138 of the NI Act. 18. I have considered the rival submissions made on behalf of all the parties and have also perused the record. The three payments i.e. of Rs. 2,00,000/­, Rs. 3,00,000/­ and Rs. 5,00,000/­ by the accused have been admitted by the complainant and even otherwise, the same have been proved by the accused by production of Ex. DW­1/1 to Ex. DW­1/6. The CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 23 of 29 statement Ex. DW­1/2 clearly shows that as on 20.02.2002, the debit balance in one of the account of the accused no. 1 firm was 10,38,433.70/­ and three cheques given by accused no. 2 on behalf of accused no. 1 firm were credited in the said account and after dishonour of the same the account was once again debited with the cheques' amount. Thereafter, the three payments made by the accused in the month of November and December 2003 were once again adjusted by the complainant in the same account. Thus the accused has sufficiently proved that they have already made the payment towards the cheques in question to the complainant. 18. Now coming to the further issue as to whether the aforesaid payment would absolve the accused of their liability under Section 138 of the NI Act read with Section 141 thereof. It has been admitted by the accused no. 2 during his cross examination that the accused have not made any payment since the dishonor of the cheques till 12.11.2003. No evidence to the contrary has been lead by accused number 3 also. While discussing the second issue, I have already held that the legal notice was duly served upon all the accused and as such it is further held that the accused have failed to make the payment towards the dishonoured cheque to the complainant within the statutory period of 15 days from the CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 24 of 29 date of service of the legal notice and as such they are not absolved of their liability under Section 138 of the NI Act, merely on account of those payments. Hence the third question is answered in the negative. (d) Whether the present complaint is not maintainable qua accused number 3 in terms of Section 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act? 19. It is submitted by Ld. Counsel for the complainant in this regard that the testimony of CW­1 to the effect that the accused number 3 was in­charge and responsible for day to day affairs of the business of accused no. 1 firm at the relevant point of time has remained un­ controverted during the cross examination of AR of the complainant and accused no. 3 has failed to lead any evidence to the contrary, other than her self serving statement to the effect that she was a sleeping partner and as such according to him, the accused no. 3 is liable under Section 138 of the NI Act read with Section 141 of the Act. On the other hand, it is submitted by Ld. Counsel for the accused, that burden to prove that accused number 3 was in­charge and responsible for conduct of day to day affairs of the business of the accused no. 1 firm was on the complainant and complainant has failed to discharge that burden and as such accused no. 3 is entitled to be acquitted. CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 25 of 29 20. I have considered the rival submissions and have perused the record. The present complaint under Section 138 of the NI Act is a criminal complaint and as per the fundamental rules of evidence the burden of proof in criminal cases is always on the complainant and complainant is required to prove all the facts constituting the offence beyond reasonable doubts. Although, there are certain presumptions in favour of the complainant under the Negotiable Instruments Act , but there is no such presumption regarding the liability of a partner who has not signed the cheque on behalf of the partnership firm. In order to convict any partner who is not the signatory of cheque in question the complaint is bound to prove that he was in­charge and responsible for day to day affairs of the business of the partnership firm or the cheque was issued in connivance or with the consent of such partner. Proof here does not mean mere reproduction of the statutory language in testimony of any of the witnesses. The complainant was liable to prove beyond reasonable doubts that accused no. 3 was in fact in­charge and responsible for day­to­day affairs of the business of accused no. 1 firm. Mere averments in the testimony of CW­1 would not suffice particularly in a case where the accused no. 3 herself had stepped into the witness box and had deposed to the effect that she was merely a sleeping partner. CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 26 of 29 The complainant has failed to place on record any document in support of its submission that accused no. 3 was in­charge and responsible for day to day affairs of accused no. 1 firm. It is true that no suggestion whatsoever was given by Ld. Counsel for accused no. 3 to CW­1 during his cross examination that accused number 3 was a sleeping partner and was not responsible for day to day affairs of the accused no. 1 firm. The aforesaid evidence could not be put to the accused during her (her AR's) examination under Section 313 Cr.P.C. when recorded for the first time and as such no evidence was led by the accused on this issue in her defence. However, this court decided to again record the statement of the accused no. 3 under section 313 of the Cr.P.C. and when the aforesaid piece of testimony of AR of the complainant was put to the accused no. 3, she had denied that she was in­charge and responsible for day to day affairs of accused no. 1 firm. She stated that she was merely a sleeping partner in the firm. She has also examined herself as DW­2 and categorically stated that she was a sleeping partner. The testimony of the accused no. 3 also withstood the test of cross examination by Ld. Counsel for the complainant and although during the cross examination it was suggested by Ld. Counsel for the complainant that accused no. 3 had signed the loan agreement with the complainant bank to which accused CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 27 of 29 no. 3 has responded­ "I do not remember". However, the complainant has deliberately withheld the aforesaid loan agreement giving rise to an adverse inference that, if produced, the same would have gone against the complainant. The complainant has failed to place on record any document signed by the accused number 3 on behalf of accused no. 1 firm. Moreover, on a perusal of the material available on record it appears that even during the pendency of the trial in the present complaint, accused number 3 did not appear even once until this court decided to re­examine her personally under Section 313 of the Cr.P.C. Till then, accused no. 3 has authorized her son, who is accused no. 2 in the present case, to represent her during the trial. Hence, it cannot be assumed by any stretch of imagination that she was in­charge and responsible for day to day affairs of the business of accused no. 1 firm. Thus the forth question is answered in the affirmative. 21. In view of the aforesaid discussions, although the complainant has proved its case u/s 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act , beyond reasonable doubts against accused no. 2 but the complainant has failed to prove that the accused no. 3 was in­charge and responsible for day to day affairs of the business of partnership firm, accused no. 1, within the meaning of provisions of Section 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. CC NO:3611/10 ICICI BANK LTD V. NATIONAL DAIRIES Judgment dated 24.12.2011 28 of 29 22. Thus the accused no. 2 is hereby convicted for offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act read with Section 141 of the Act, while the accused no. 3 is acquitted of charges under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. Complaint qua accused no. 1 is hereby dismissed since accused no. 1 firm being a partnership firm is not a legal entity separate from its partners and hence the complaint against accused no. 1 is not maintainable. 23.
